premises: DFT-derived atomic-scale descriptors (elastic constants, misfit volumes) can serve as effective input features for an ML model predicting mechanical properties of HEAs.
Microstructural features (phase fractions, precipitate morphology) of a hierarchical heterostructure can be quantified and used as ML input features.
An ML model trained on such features can predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness of HfNbTiVAl10 with <15% error.
The ML model will achieve at least a 10× speedup over conventional full-scale DFT or FE simulations.
The cited evidence demonstrates the feasibility of ML for predicting HEA mechanical properties and the role of microstructure in HEA behavior.
